title: The expected value of a ticket in a charity raffle
intro:
An illustrative raffle, made up for this book. A charity sells 2,000 raffle tickets at $5. Prizes: one of $1,000, two of $250 and ten of $50. A ticket's net gain is the prize minus the $5 it cost.

| Net gain ($) | 995 | 245 | 45 | −5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 0.0005 | 0.001 | 0.005 | 0.9935 |

Give the expected net gain of one ticket and its standard deviation (two decimals). What does the expected value say about the raffle as a way to make money (as opposed to giving to the charity)?

In the Workbench: **Discrete distribution**, **Distribution** *Typed table of (x, P(x))*.
hints: The prizes total $2,000 of the $10,000 taken in: on average each ticket returns $1 of its $5.
